title: Buaflow operational readiness v1
description: The backup and restore procedure with the rehearsal that proves it, and the incident hooks as a contract rather than a runbook paragraph. Every hook says what detects it, how bad it is, who owns it, and which runbook section the responder opens first — and the validator checks that the detector and the section both still exist.

owner.description: Who runs backups in production. A reference app that does not own production backups says so here rather than leaving the field out.

rehearsal.description: The transcript of an actual destroy-and-restore. The validator recomputes its digest and reads its verdict, so a failed rehearsal cannot be cited as a passing one.

signal.description: The observable condition, specific enough that someone could build an alert from it without asking a follow-up question.

detectedBy.description: What produces the signal — the health endpoint, the logger, a test. Files must exist, so a hook cannot point at a detector that was deleted.

firstResponse.description: file.md#anchor pointing at the runbook section a responder opens first. Both the file and the heading are checked.

boundary.description: The trust boundary in docs/evidence/security-baseline.json this hook watches, when that record exists.
